seal.statement: The retrospective verification of formation-sim-production-replica-composition (2026-09-18, reject) found its claim of unchanged production defaults false on two production paths. (1) Since 35992c315, extended in 3f953614a and 6c8b4a841 and copied into the size-update hop by 9a39af51b, every replica the seed hosts during bootstrap is handed the node runtime's TimeSource, which is a RealTimeSource when none was supplied, so in production all seed-hosted message-group and partition replicas behave as if they owned a clock: LifeRaft runs on VirtualTick instead of tick-tock, and the commit-apply yield, the peer-reconciliation hop and the size-update hop run as setTimeout(0) instead of setImmediate, while joiner-hosted replicas do not. (2) Since 35992c315 ServiceReconciler's per-action yield is setTimeout(0) on every node where it was setImmediate. This quest restores production scheduling: a replica and the reconciler take their scheduling from a clock only when the node runtime was explicitly supplied one, and a production node, whose runtime resolved its own real clock, schedules exactly as before E - tick-tock timers and setImmediate hops, identically for seed-hosted and joiner-hosted replicas. Stamps may keep reading the node's TimeSource, whose real now() is the host clock. The simulator keeps what E built: with a supplied clock every hosted replica and the reconciler still schedule on it and the deterministic guard still reports no ambient read. It also adds the two reconcile-queue witnesses owed by formation-sim-rebalancer-current-work-completion: the draining clause of the idle predicate, and shutdown() clearing draining synchronously and releasing current-work waiters.

text:
Production scheduling restored at one seam, and the reconcile-queue witnesses added.

WHAT CHANGED (src)

1. src/node/node-runtime-local-authorities.js - the one place that answers
   "was this node runtime SUPPLIED a clock": readNodeRuntimeSuppliedTimeSource(runtime)
   returns the given clock or null. ensureNodeLocalSystemTableCache now asks it
   for ownsClock instead of reading runtime.providedTimeSource itself, so the
   fact has exactly one reader-of-record. No consumer inspects a TimeSource's
   type or identity anywhere.

2. src/bootstrap/shared/hosted-replica-authorities.js - resolveHostedReplicaAuthorities
   now spreads delegates.getSuppliedTimeSource() (the given clock, else undefined)
   rather than delegates.getTimeSource() (which resolves a RealTimeSource in
   production). This single line is what made every seed-hosted replica behave as
   if it owned a clock: with it, PartitionService/MessageGroupService
   providedTimeSource is null in production, so LifeRaft keeps tick-tock and the
   peer-reconciliation hop, the size-update hop and the commit-apply yield keep
   setImmediate - identically to a joiner-hosted replica. Nothing else in the
   replica changed; stamps still resolve a real clock whose now() is the host clock.

3. src/bootstrap/bootstrap-service-seed-delegates.js and
   src/bootstrap/phases/seed-infrastructure-phase.js - both delegate bundles gain
   getSuppliedTimeSource, answered by the owner function above. getTimeSource stays
   for the stamping/waiting sites (resolveHostedNodeClock, the lifecycle manager).

4. src/bootstrap/shared/startup-service-lifecycle-owner.js - the ServiceReconciler
   is constructed with timeSource: delegates.getSuppliedTimeSource?.(), so in
   production it is offered no clock (its pre-E shape) and in the simulator it is
   offered the node's virtual clock. The ServiceLifecycleManager keeps getTimeSource:
   it only stamps.

5. src/service/service-reconciler.js - resolveOwnedTimeSource splits the two
   questions: _timeSource (resolved; the cadence and cycle stamps are byte-identical
   to before) and _providedTimeSource (given or null). The per-action macrotask
   boundary moved into yieldPerActionTurn(providedTimeSource): the supplied clock
   when there is one, otherwise setImmediate - which is what it was before
   35992c315, on every node, seed or joiner.

6. src/bootstrap/bootstrap-service-runtime-methods.js - the shutdown yield reads the
   same owner function instead of nodeService.providedTimeSource directly.

No timeout, delay, interval, retry or budget value changed.

WHAT CHANGED (tests)

test/bootstrap/production-scheduling-defaults.test.js (new) holds four witnesses.
Each one composes a real BootstrapService the way lagrange-runtime-startup.js does
(its own NodeService, no clock), takes the authorities a seed phase spreads, builds
a real PartitionService (in-memory db, initialize()) and a real MessageGroupService
from them, and records which host primitive production actually armed by replacing
globalThis.setImmediate/setTimeout for the duration of one call (pass-through, host
primitives captured at module load). The commit-apply yield is driven through the
exported commitEntriesCooperatively on the replica's own LifeRaft timer manager with
a log that commits one entry per slice, so the loop must take exactly one
inter-slice yield.

- "a seed-hosted replica schedules like a production replica": authorities carry no
  clock; raft.timers is not a VirtualTick; the peer hop, the size hop and the
  commit-apply yield each arm exactly [setImmediate]; a seed-hosted message-group
  replica's hop does too. Red before the repair: authorities.timeSource was a
  RealTimeSource (and the hops armed setTimeout(0), the timers were VirtualTick).
- "a seed-hosted and a joiner-hosted replica schedule alike": the same node's
  seed-authority replica and a no-authority replica are compared directly - timer
  manager class, both hops, the commit-apply yield, and the message-group hop.
  Red before: VirtualTick vs Tick.
- "a production reconciler takes each per-action turn on setImmediate": the real
  reconciler the seed infrastructure phase builds executes a two-action plan (a
  service type with no adapter, so the actions fail and nothing is created; the turn
  is taken either way) and arms [setImmediate, setImmediate]; so does a reconciler
  constructed with no clock offered. Red before: [setTimeout(0), setTimeout(0)].
- "a supplied clock still owns hosted replica and reconciler scheduling": a
  NodeService given a recording clock; authorities carry that clock, raft.timers is
  a VirtualTick, both hops and the commit-apply yield arm nothing on the host and
  exactly two zero-delay arms land on the clock, the message-group hop likewise, and
  the reconciler the same phase builds takes one zero-delay turn per action on the
  clock and never a setImmediate. Green before and after: E's simulator behaviour is
  what this holds fixed.

The four witnesses share one recorder, so they are one file: a second copy of the
recorder raised the test duplication ratchet by one clone group, and test/helpers is
outside this quest's authorized paths.

test/workflow/owner-key-reconcile-queue-current-work.test.js gains the two witnesses
formation-sim-rebalancer-current-work-completion owed:
- "Q6. a drain that has been scheduled but not run is still current work" pins the
  draining clause in the one state that isolates it: a retryable reconcile absorbs
  the item enqueued while it ran into its retry item (pending empties), the drain
  that enqueue scheduled has not run, inFlight is empty - and the queue must still
  not read as idle. Q2 cannot pin the clause because there pending alone answers.
- "Q7. shutdown clears draining and releases current-work waiters" pins the
  shutdown change: draining is false synchronously after shutdown() and the waiter
  settles instead of being left unsettleable.

MUTATION (each receipt red when its repair is reverted)
- hosted-replica-authorities back to getTimeSource(): receipts 1 and 2 red.
- service-reconciler yield back to this._timeSource.setTimeout(resolve, 0): receipt 3 red.
- startup owner back to delegates.getTimeSource?.(): receipt 3 red.
- readNodeRuntimeSuppliedTimeSource returning runtime.getTimeSource(): receipt 1 red.
- the draining clause removed from isReconcileQueueCurrentWorkIdle: Q6 red, Q7 green.
- the two shutdown lines removed: Q7 red, Q6 green.

round 1 APPROVE (no blocking findings). Measured on a production-shaped node (BootstrapService with no nodeService option, NodeService singleton, providedTimeSource null), recording the host primitive each site actually armed, against git-archive snapshots of pre-E (3e52cd3a0^) and post-E (HEAD): the seed partition and message-group replicas' LifeRaft timer manager (Tick / VirtualTick / Tick), the partition and message-group peer-reconciliation hops, the size-update hop from 9a39af51b and the commit-apply yield (setImmediate / setTimeout(0) / setImmediate), the seed and the joiner ServiceReconciler per-action yield (setImmediate / setTimeout(0) / setImmediate); joiner-hosted replicas, the bootstrap shutdown yield and the node-local cache hop unchanged throughout. Every changed line of git diff 3e52cd3a0^ HEAD -- src/ (99 files) that mentions a scheduling primitive was listed: those six are the only non-equivalent rewrites and all six return to pre-E; every other rewrite substitutes a RealTimeSource that delegates to the globals. No site moved to a third behaviour. Own RealTimeSource per replica: pre-E replicas held no TimeSource at all; RealTimeSource is stateless; src has no TimeSource identity comparison, instanceof or constructor.name check. The rejection's four probes run against the staged tree read: authority timeSource null, Tick, setImmediate everywhere. Simulator unchanged: with a supplied clock HEAD and staged are identical on every seed-path site; host transcript, network transcript, strict report and provenance digests IDENTICAL for the phase-one, message-group, partition and handoff scenarios, uncharged and charged; the four probes read 0 (charged seed host 3m19s behind the thermal gate); the 13 other simulation test files pass. One owner: the only reader of a node runtime's providedTimeSource outside NodeService is readNodeRuntimeSuppliedTimeSource. 15 mutations, each restored with the index tree unchanged: reverts of each repair turn exactly their receipts red, three over-repairs (authorities never carry a clock, reconciler always setImmediate, owner always null) turn receipt 4 red, a replica treating its resolved clock as provided turns receipt 1 red (the witness measures the armed primitive, not the field), and the four queue mutations turn only Q6 or Q7 red. 32 owner-tree files pass one at a time including control-plane, rebalancer and harness samples the implementer had not run; pre-commit exits 0 with the index unchanged; complexity 1819/1819, cognitive 160/160, audit:shards, unused:push, file-size, cycles, duplication and boundary-mode contracts green. The attempt text is accurate; no timing constant changed. Non-blocking: the witness comment says the BootstrapService is composed with its own NodeService where production takes the singleton (same fact under test); the message-group LifeRaft timer class is asserted only indirectly; the rerouted shutdown yield and cache ownsClock have no dedicated red-on-revert witness (both behaviour-preserving); two stale comments in untouched seed-phase files; E's unconditional LifeRaft.clone remote-peer representation remains, outside this statement and already verified separately (6bbf95092); a simulated joiner's reconciler would still yield on a host primitive, which no simulator artifact exercises.
